summary: The proof passes sequential verification. Step 1 correctly computes the Gauss-sum valuations, justifies uniform convergence and analytic continuation, and obtains nonzero residues 2 and 1 for the two normalized projections; the continuation domain matches [Besser–de Jeu, Theorem 2.7(3)](https://research.vu.nl/ws/portalfiles/portal/2459860/220267.pdf). Step 2 satisfies the special-unit and cocycle conditions in [Besser–de Jeu, Theorems 1.6 and 1.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0110334). Clearing denominators and applying 1−sigma_(-1) produce an actual integral class with the asserted reduction and antisymmetry. Step 3 uses a comparison valid without a ramification restriction in [Huber–Kings, Section 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0612611). The finite-coefficient construction is additive, natural and compatible with reduction and transitions by [Weibel, Section 2](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/archive/papers-dir/chernclass.pdf); the inverse-limit argument establishes the required Q_5-linear map without assuming surjectivity from actual K-theory. Step 4 correctly applies the finite-field vanishing and [AMMN, Theorem A, Corollary 3.8 and Proposition 4.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.12541). The resulting equivariant comparison transfers both nonvanishing conclusions to b. All projectors act on Q_5-vector-space targets. No critical error, proof gap or hard-prohibition violation was found.
